---

## Law of the face (short)

1. **Sequence is blank.** An agent sequence is a container. It can hold **multiple goals** (multiple campaigns). Not one-objective-or-nothing.
2. **Two objectives → two campaigns.** If you want two things met, each requires its own campaign. When a campaign’s **objective is met**, you may string the next campaign. There is **no “first objective”** object. The distance between campaigns is **not** a qualify node.
3. **Opt-in (the teaching example):** **Launch window** and **Launch day** are **campaign names** we used so the first pictures had something in them. The operator can rename both. Window builds desire (why we don’t start at reactivation). Launch day, in that example, is opt-in day. That pair is **not** a frozen system type.
4. **Campaigns have objectives. Channels do not.** Channels are the **medium**. **Channel rules = escalation on that medium** (not opened, not clicked, …). **Attempt rules are not at the channel.** An attempt is a **container / cycle** of the same sequence.
5. **Sequencing lives at campaign level** (“how many channels here, in what order”) — not at the channel node.
6. **Content lives inside the channel node** as an **Override content toggle**. On → the node **expands** to contain that medium’s content-creation block (SMS composer, email composer, call script). Not a wired sibling. Not a small button. Attempt-specific copy is a **variation on that same node**.
7. **Override this** is the first toggle on a campaign. It **opens the campaign** and **reveals channel nodes as wires**. Campaign-level toggles **stay on the campaign**. Open a channel → **channel rules** (escalation) hang off as the channel’s deeper grain. Content stays inside.
8. **Rules nest like CSS.** Global (Agents module Settings) → sequence Settings → campaign if overridden → channel. If you do not override, fall back up.
9. **Attempt rules sit where their grain is.** Per **campaign** → on that campaign (visible, no gray area). Per **sequence** → **Sequence Settings** modal, not in the middle of the canvas. **Global** → **Agents Settings**. Do not draw attempt cycles between campaigns.
10. **Empty world:** no templates until someone authors them. Opt-in / re-engagement / reactivation are **sequence templates** (the full canvas), not objective names.
11. **Objective ≠ sequence.** Objective = **one campaign**. Sequences have templates; objectives have templates. You do not put “opt-in” in the objective picker.
12. **First thing on a campaign is the objective.** Hub Automations: trigger node → **Add configuration**. Same seat, not the same module — do not import Automations triggers onto this canvas.
13. **Untemplated objective is a binary event** (word “event” may change). One yes/no: everyone enrolled is campaigned to do **this one thing**. Happened or it didn’t. Then you name it. Templated objective populates the rest of that campaign.
14. **Enroll lives on this sequence’s Contacts.** That model **displays who is enrolled**. **Add contact** is the hand door, and it lives in the **sequence header** — same row as Save / Launch agent — always there, not inside the Contacts tab body. Same Add-contact grain also lives in **Automations** (**A19** — same look). **Select from** opens the list (**C8b**). Scope is **two**, not three: **Every firm** (top, default) or **Select from** (bottom — list opens with everyone selected; deselect to pick a specific contact). No separate “this firm” / “this contact” radios. **Not Publish.** Automations enroll is the other door (on an event). Agents enroll **starts the mission now** — it is not waiting on a current event.
15. **Activity / engagement chart ≠ lineage query.** The engagement chart is a **tree of outreach**. It does **not** connect left to the trigger or event that created the agent or assigned it to the objective. Keep that chart pristine. Who created / path / completion / time is **queryable** (Automations law 29) — a different thing.
16. **Captions on the plates are not spec.** Teaching copy (“qualify — first objective met,” “they opt in,” “smallest workflow…”) was for the founder to read the picture. Audit: [`IMAGE-CAPTION-AUDIT.md`](./IMAGE-CAPTION-AUDIT.md). Do not mint nodes or fields from those sentences. A tick on “objective met” between campaigns is allowed chrome. It is still not a node.

---

## What you are authoring (the package)

An **agent** is still the 15:43 thing. The **sequence** is a **blank container** for campaigns (goals). The **canvas** is how that looks.

```
SEQUENCE TEMPLATE  (blank canvas — opt-in / re-engagement / reactivation)
│
├─ Campaign  = one OBJECTIVE
│    [ first thing: the objective ]
│         pick a template  → populates the campaign
│         or from scratch  → binary event (yes/no), then name it
│    sequencing (channel order / how many channels)     ← campaign level
│    rules fall back: campaign override → sequence Settings → Agents Settings
│    attempt rules when per-campaign live ON this campaign
│    [ Override this ]  → reveals wired CHANNEL nodes
│         └─ Channel node  (medium: text / email / form)
│              [ Override content ]  ← TOGGLE INSIDE the node; on → node expands
│                   to the content-creation block for that medium
│                   variation at attempt N  (same node, same sequence cycle)
│              channel rules = escalation (not opened, not clicked, …)
│                   hang off this node when you open the channel
│              attempt rules do NOT live here
│
│    Attempt = a cycle of this campaign’s sequence work
│         after last node fails → next attempt
│         attempt rules at sequence/global → Settings modals, not the canvas middle
│
├─ Contacts   = who is enrolled on THIS sequence
│    displays enrolled
│    Add contact lives in the sequence HEADER (same row as Save / Launch)
│         not inside the Contacts tab body
│    scope: Every firm (default) · Select from (all selected; deselect to pick one)
│    same grain in Automations / events
│    starts the mission now (not an event, not Publish)
│
└─ next Campaign  (when the previous campaign’s objective is met — not a qualify node)
```

**Opt-in — example campaigns on that sequence (names are ours; operator can rename):**

| Campaign name (example) | Binary (from-scratch shape in the example) | Why we used it in the picture |
|----------|-----------|----------------|
| **Launch window** | Spoken: probably **click this link** | Build desire. Why we don’t start at reactivation. **A name, not a type.** |
| **Launch day** | They opt in — **a title at best**, not an objective class | In the example, opt-in day. Justified because the previous objective was met. |
| **Additional** | Unnamed here | Founder: there are a couple more in this sequence. C2 row stays disabled. |

Between campaigns: **objective met → you may string the next.** That distance may show a tick. It is **not** a qualify node and **not** “first objective.” See [`IMAGE-CAPTION-AUDIT.md`](./IMAGE-CAPTION-AUDIT.md).

Picking a **templated** objective populates everything related to that template. From scratch: configure the binary event, then name it.

Spoken ladder in this mock: **text → email → call** (call via ElevenLabs). Stood-up machine still has form; do not silently drop form from the machine. Call is now on the face because the founder asked to see the node.

That is **not** four emails in one Timeline. Flattening it is the miss.

---

## Defaults and overrides (every rule)

**There is a default on every single rule.** Failure rules are **part of escalation rules** — not a separate authored family that splits the 15:43 flag into “actions on goals.”

| Rule family | What it is | Where it lives |
|-------------|------------|----------------|
| **Channel rules** | Escalation on that medium (not opened, not clicked, …) | Channel node when opened. Fallback: campaign → sequence Settings → Agents Settings (global) |
| **Attempt rules** | Number of attempts; cycle; distance after the failed last node; optional nth-attempt exception | **Per campaign:** on that campaign. **Per sequence:** Sequence Settings. **Global:** Agents Settings. Never in the middle of the canvas. Never on the channel. |
| **Content** | What goes out on that medium | **Button inside the channel node.** Editor opens in the node. Sequence / global possible via that sequence’s Settings / Agents Settings. Attempt = a variation on the same node. |
| **Sequencing** | How many channels, order | Campaign |
| **Campaign objective** | The one yes/no | The campaign itself. When met, you may string the next campaign |

`firm_sequence_binding` + `rule_*.firm_id` NULL remains firm vs platform. In-package override is this graph, not a second Settings list.

**Where toggles sit (after Override this):**

| Layer | UI |
|-------|-----|
| **Global** | Agents **module** Settings |
| **Sequence** | **That sequence’s** Settings |
| **Campaign** | On the campaign node (sequencing, Override this). Campaign can override sequence/global. |
| **Channel** | Channel rules (escalation) hang off the open channel. **Override content** is a button **inside** the node. |
| **Attempt** | Not that stack. A cycle of the same sequence. Content variation on the channel node. |

Fallback is CSS-like: no override → sequence → global.

---

## Canvas behaviour — Override this (the graph)

Closed: campaign nodes on the sequence. Between campaigns: previous **objective met** (tick / chrome allowed). That distance is **not** a qualify node.

On each campaign, **one first toggle at the bottom: Override this.**

| Click | What happens |
|-------|----------------|
| **Override this** | Opens that campaign. **Reveals channel nodes as wires**. Campaign-level toggles **remain on the campaign**. |
| Open a **channel** | **Channel rules** (escalation) hang off as wired deeper grain. **Override content** is a small button **inside** the channel — editor opens in the node (text, or the email composer). **Attempt rules do not appear here.** |

Do not replace the campaign with a Timeline. The campaign stays; the channels **hang off it**.

**Today:** generated images. Beat 5 revised: content inside the node; attempt rules off the channel.

---

## Mock map (what you said → what you can see)

Not one picture. Five beats, one labeled mock. Objective is a **modal** on the canvas (same idea as Hub Add configuration). Sequence templates are their own beat because that picker is a different layer.

| Beat | What you said | Same mock or own |
|------|----------------|------------------|
| **1. Sequence templates** | Empty world; opt-in / re-engagement / reactivation are sequence templates, not objectives | Own beat (different picker) |
| **2. Add objective** | First thing on a campaign. Template (example names: launch window, launch day, additional) vs from scratch (click / calendar / form, then name it) | **Modal** on the canvas |
| **3. Two campaigns** | Two objectives → two campaigns. Distance = previous objective met (not a qualify node). In the example, Launch day = opt-in day | Canvas |
| **4. Override this** | First toggle. Reveals text / email / form as wires. Campaign toggles stay | Canvas |
| **5. Open a channel** | Channel rules (escalation) hang off. Content = button inside. Attempt rules are not here | Canvas expand |

Webhook / table lookup is named, not mocked. Call channel is not mocked.

---

## Objective first (binary event) — two template layers

Hub Automations (`/hub`): empty canvas → add a trigger → on that node, **Add configuration** (event configuration). Campaign authorship uses the same *seat*: the first thing on a campaign is the **objective**. That is not a license to put Automations triggers on the Agents canvas.

**From scratch:** the untemplated objective looks like an event (name may change). Everyone enrolled in this campaign is campaigned to do **one thing**. Yes or no. Then you name it.

| Spoken from-scratch | Binary |
|---------------------|--------|
| Click this link | Did they, or not |
| Book a meeting in this calendar | Did they, or not |
| Submit / complete this form | Did they, or not |
| Later: webhook / table (name in a list) | Did they, or not — do not mint now |

**From a template:** pick an **objective template** (a campaign, e.g. launch window). It populates everything related to that template. You do not pick “opt-in” here — that is a **sequence template**.

Empty world: no templates exist until authored. Keep that in the open.

---

## Further enrichment (agent alignment — not a second flag)

Founder: “I’m not circling, I’m enriching, and I think you can even further enrich.” This section is that enrichment. It does not replace 15:43 or the excerpts above.

**The agent is a sequence, not a campaign.** The list item (Opt-in, Nudge, Reactivation) is a **blank sequence**. Campaigns live inside it. Opt-in is the teaching case because it already needs **two** objectives, therefore **two** campaigns.

**Why a launch window exists (the meta-reason).** We do not start at reactivation. In the teaching example, the window’s job is to **build desire** for opt-in, and Launch day **is** opt-in day. Those are **names**. The next campaign is justified because the previous campaign’s **objective was met**. That is the 15:43 “goal is itself an escalation point” — the distance between campaigns, not a Settings row, not a fourth channel, and **not** a qualify node. The C3 pill was a founder caption. See [`IMAGE-CAPTION-AUDIT.md`](./IMAGE-CAPTION-AUDIT.md).

**One thing in the window.** Not the waitlist question. The window’s objective is still **one binary event** — everyone enrolled is campaigned to do that one yes/no. Spoken from-scratch for the window: probably **click this link**. Do not split the window into two campaigns unless there are two objectives.

**Two template layers.** Sequence templates = the full canvas (opt-in, re-engagement, reactivation). Objective templates = a single campaign (launch window, launch day, plus additional unnamed in opt-in). Empty world: no templates until authored. Keep that in the open.

**First thing on a campaign is the objective.** Same *seat* as Hub Automations (`/hub`): you add a trigger, then on that node **Add configuration**. Here you add a campaign, then the first thing on it is the objective. Do **not** put Automations triggers on this canvas.

**Untemplated objective = binary event** (the word “event” may change). Click this link · book this calendar · submit this form. Happened or it didn’t. Then you name it. Webhook / table lookup (name in a list → completed) is down the line; the system should not be so complicated that it is impossible. Do not mint that now.

**Toggle locality (law of the graph).** A toggle lives at the layer it governs and **does not migrate** when the graph opens.

| If the toggle is about… | It lives… | After Override this |
|-------------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| The campaign as a whole (sequencing, the objective, Override this) | On the campaign node | **Still on the campaign** |

---

## Law of the face (short)

1. **Agents (creation place) is left complete enough.** Operator authors **campaigns** there. Automations is the **brain / operations**. Do not grow Agents to invent forms.
2. **Automations shape (definite middle):** **On this event** (schedule or trigger) → **perform this operation** (the middle does not change; it is definite) → **on this kind of result do X / on that kind do Y**. Results are **binary** (or the binaries we have defined). More **DAG-like** than Agents’ sequence canvas.
3. **Exit points** sit at the **end of that operation**, per instance that ran.
4. **Re-engagement is not an objective.** It is a **campaign** (the name of a campaign). Already Agents law: opt-in / re-engagement / reactivation are **sequence templates**. An automation does not “trigger a re-engagement objective.”
5. **What an automation typically originates** is a **data request** objective — fill this form with these questions — **not** “click this button.” Maybe other objective types. Click-this still lives on **Agents** (launch window). Automations would not trigger it.
6. **The form is created in Automations.** Agents is not about creating forms or creating what is needed. Agents is about **sending people to accomplish the goal**. How Automations works the form has nothing to do with Agents.
7. **Recursive join:** a **data request is already an event of origin for Agents**. Data request = a form, handled by Automations. The Automations **end node** (start / select an agent) **mirrors** the Agents **beginning** (declare the objective).
8. **Same end node (leaning embedded):** assign an agent **or** instantiate from a template, **and** declare the objective right there. If that objective is a data request, **create the form in that same node**. Form-as-its-own-graph-node vs embedded-with-calling-the-agent is **not locked** — founder leans **embedded**. **00:02:** you do **not** author a new agent in this module (law 31).
9. **Select an agent = the whole sequence.** Campaigns live **inside** sequences. No separate campaign picker on that node. Campaigns can be templated. **Which agents you may select is limited by the objective** — can be enforced.
10. **Automation may trigger creation of a campaign** when a **templated** campaign already exists for that objective. That is enroll / instantiate, not Agents growing a form builder.
11. **Hub is the complete Automations module.** Current-app / CT Ant Automations was **born from Hub**. It is a **translation** (same kind) and a **poor rendition of quality**. Work from Hub nodes. Do not “fix” Ant independently as if it were the source.
12. **Look at Rules to see the end goal.** Plate: Hub → Automations → **New firm → opt-in launch** → Rule **Immigration · Service eligibility**. Open it: **toggles** on outcome families (Pathway detection, Gaps, Profile & operations, Category draws, Draw competitiveness). Under the hood: conditions against constants. A **rule is a composite of conditions and constants**. Rules are **creatable**. Modular **across industries**.
13. **Easy to miss because it touches more of the app.** Something comes in (outreach, existing data, other sources) → perform an operation → **actions are not only outreach**. Outcomes also **change stuff inside the system**.
14. **Not limited to code.** PM verdict: the authored logic **is simple enough for a GUI**. A condition is field · operator · constant. A rule is togglable families of those. Under-the-hood evaluator stays code. **Two options:** **GUI** (default where possible) · **Custom** (code / JSON when the GUI isn’t enough).
15. **Smallest workflow = trigger · rule · action.** A rule lets us create the smallest looking automation. Then name the pieces and build them separately.
16. **This Rule part does not exist in the Ant translation.** Image mocks are **from scratch** in Ant chrome. Mock = generate the image. See [`AUTOMATIONS-UI-BLUEPRINT.md`](./AUTOMATIONS-UI-BLUEPRINT.md).
17. **Inside a rule, outcomes can be GUI or named code.** Where a constant can be referenced, GUI (prefer always defining a constant when possible). Where no constant can be referenced — especially across industries — it is **named code** (JavaScript or Python), **created in the rules module**, not hard-coded. It still **toggles on or off**. You name it. Side-by-side with GUI outcomes. (Whole-rule Custom/JSON remains the escape hatch for the entire rule.)
18. **Look inside trigger and inside action.** Add a node, select Action as a node. Not satisfied with canvas-only.
19. **At least two kinds of actions:** (a) **in the application** — change something inside the system from the operation; (b) **agents** — send people to a goal.
20. **Agents as the action:** select an agent, or create / select the objective. Creating the objective probably **creates the form** (already Automations-owns-the-form).
21. **A rule can emit re-engagement and/or reactivation as signals — one, the other, or both at once.** Do not split the rule to separate them. That is why we can have **different actions**. Engine 2 already: every detection is a signal; outreach is one motion (reactivation first; nudge only if not; secondary attaches as agenda).
22. **Rule output classes are a lattice.** They all need to exist. Each class is something you can put a simple **condition** on, and that **forks actions** — including three kinds of actions on the **same data** (example: if re-engagement signal · if **only** re-engagement signal · if **anything other than that**).
23. **At least one class is missing: required data.** When the system knows data is required, that is a re-engagement signal **and** it must be an output class. Forms are built from that set — the questions **are** the required fields. Do **not** lock an objective type to a given signal; you can still create the objective.
24. **This loop is deterministic.** Seed already: collectible field class (self-reportable / document-dependent / employer-directed); every missing-data detection is a signal; nudge consolidates outstanding self-reportable needs into **one** form. No AI to decide what data is required. If that ever stops being true, say so.
25. **Required data as a class is a listing, not a flag — and it is not stood up.** The data being requested is **more than one** item. A catalog of collectible fields exists in code (`COLLECTIBLE_FIELDS`) and is **unused**. Rule-node output today is headline / pass / pathway & gap **result ids** / services / nudge & reactivation **signals** — not a list of requested fields. No UI lists that request. No form authoring **references** those ids. Contact forms that look like a list are painted demos. Until the listing is on rule output, a form cannot bind to it. Do not invent the rest of the catalog; do not mint tables.
26. **Two grains of condition. Do not collapse them.** Inside the rule: field · operator · constant (or named code). After the rule, on the DAG: a **condition / If node** that **calls from the previous result** (rule Output) and forks actions. Hub already has that If node. A10 / A13 are **diagrams of the lattice idea**, not a screenshot of that node, and not a screen to build. Founder 22:17: A13 is a different kind of picture.
27. **An event has a global grain and a local grain. That is not “Settings.”** Form completion **is** an event that can trigger an automation. **Global:** on all form submissions of that kind — whoever submitted, run this evaluation. **Local:** on **this** form — every time this specific form is submitted, run this evaluation. The same divide is why Automations needs a global/local place (it matches Agents’ global → sequence → campaign, without copying a Settings modal). This expands **what counts as an event**. Do not invent the rest of the event catalog this stamp. Do not call it Settings.
28. **No special return.** The return **is** an event. **All objectives are events.** The write-back **is** the event; the event happening **is** the write-back. It is detected across the app / in the database. It is not lost. Loop 1 (23:07) is settled this way — not a separate return wire.
29. **Lineage is queryable at the minimum.** What created the objective (agent-created or hand-created). The path that agent took from that creation to completion. The completion event. Time it took. Map it correctly. That is querying, not a new module. If it is not queryable, the loop is not real.
30. **Campaign failure is an event.** Global and local apply (all campaign failures vs **this** campaign). Then an **in-app action**: create a record — even as simple as **ascribe a tag**. Named example: the subscription bell (subscribed / not) **is a tag** created in Automations. Opt-out / unsubscribe is also an event; it assigns that tag. Campaign fails → ascribes that tag. This is one of the first in-app actions named. Do not invent the rest of the action catalog.
31. **Automations does not create agents.** Create the agent in **Agents**, then **assign**. On the Agents action there are two choices: **assign to an existing sequence**, or **create from a template**. No third choice: author a new agent here. Can evolve later — not now. Plate **A14**. A8 stays prior for select-agent = whole sequence. A12 stays the form. The sequence pick (Opt-in / Re-engagement / Reactivation) is a **radio**. There is **nothing further** — no chevron, no extra configuration. Add-contact scope is the same two as C8 (**Every firm** default, or **Select from**) and also lives on **events**. **A19** is Automations Contacts — same look. **Select from** opens the list (**C8b**). **A18** is Global vs Local on the **event**. Global/local of the event is also **dependent on which contacts are enrolled**. Automations still does **not** start a mission right now — that is Agents (C8).
32. **Automations is a blank canvas, the same way an agent is.** Smallest workflow is still trigger · rule · action. The canvas can **chain**: event → action → condition on that output → another action. Teaching walk: **firm created / provisioned** → **audit the contacts** → **if X** (condition node, previous result) → **agents**. Provisioning a firm is not only creating the firm — things inside still have to happen; that is why this module exists. The If node already named (law 26) can read an **action’s** output, not only a rule’s. Completion of a step is also an event (law 28), so the same chain can be one canvas or two automations listening. Do not collapse those. Do not put this chain on the Agents canvas.
33. **When a node finishes, you have every write that run made.** The action sends the work to the **real** module. The next step **picks** which of those writes it is about. Not a boolean “done.” Not a short list we specified. Not “Audit is two things” and “Provision is a firm.” Same shape for every action. Live is SA **015** — engineer is cutting it. Hub preview is not the live path. [`PRIMITIVES.md`](./PRIMITIVES.md).

---

## What you are authoring (the package)

An **automation** is not an agent sequence. Sketch (20:24 DAG still stands; Hub **Rules** are the interior of the operation to look at):

```
BLANK CANVAS  (same idea as a blank sequence — you can chain)

EVENT  (schedule | trigger)
  e.g. firm created / provisioned
  → ACTION     (in the application — e.g. audit the contacts)
       OUTPUT  (previous result)
  → CONDITION / If   (calls from that output; if X)
  → ACTION     (agents — assign existing or from a template)
                 selecting an agent = the whole sequence

Smallest still legal: trigger · rule · action
The rule can sit in the chain wherever the operation is.
If reads the previous result — rule or action.
```

**Inside the operation, look at Rules** (Hub plate — Immigration · Service eligibility):

```
RULE  (creatable; industry-modular)
  = composite of CONDITIONS + CONSTANTS
  operator toggles outcome families on/off
  input  ← outreach / existing data / other sources
  output → analysis + actions
             actions ≠ only outreach
             also outcomes that change stuff inside the system
```

Agents still owns: campaigns, sequencing, channel/attempt/content, sending people to the goal.  
Automations owns: the event, the operation (rules / constants / conditions as Hub built them), the binary exits, the form (data request), handing into an agent, **and in-system outcomes**.

---

## What this is not

- Not overwriting 15:43. Not restoring 14:58. Not putting Automations **triggers** on the Agents canvas.
- Not treating “re-engagement” as an objective. Not treating opt-in / reactivation that way either.
- Not moving form creation into Agents. Not making Agents a form builder.
- Not treating **Hub as the app**. Product face = CT Ant. Hub is the **advanced plant** for Automations/Rules — look at it for that grain, not as if it were the product.
- Not treating **CT Ant** Automations as the source plant for Rules. Hub is that plant. Ant is the translation.
- Not throwing away Hub’s node kinds (rule / constant / condition). Rules with toggles **are** the end-goal grain to look at.
- Not locking form-as-node vs embedded — lean is embedded; still named open.
- Not a full catalog of operations or exit points. “Add them to …” was not finished. Name the silence.
- Not minting tables. SA extract after this face is specified enough — same discipline as Agents.
- Not a UI blueprint of the whole DAG. Smallest workflow first: [`AUTOMATIONS-UI-BLUEPRINT.md`](./AUTOMATIONS-UI-BLUEPRINT.md). Mock = generate the image. Do not plant `AntAutomationWorkbench` this pass.
- Not generating or refining A9/A10 until asked. 21:36 answered the listing question first. A11–A13 mock the listing (Output rows, form bind, lattice **diagram**). A13 is not a screen. Do not plant the editor.
- Not collapsing inside-the-rule conditions with the If node after the previous result.
- Not treating Automations as a one-shot (trigger · rule · action only). That is the smallest. The canvas can chain (law 32).
- Not inventing an Automations **Settings** modal. Global vs local is the divide (law 27). Not filling an event catalog.
- Not **creating agents** inside Automations. Assign existing, or from a template (law 31 / A14).
- Not circling **pipe vs this-then-that**. The product is the handle after the node (law 33). Live is not that yet. Do not treat Hub preview as the live path.

---

## Open (tinkering — do not fill)

1. Full list of **operations** Automations performs (data request is one; engagement was spoken as a maybe).
2. Full list of **exit points** besides start/select agent.
3. Form creation: **own graph node** vs **embedded** in the start-agent node (lean: embedded).
4. When an automation starts a campaign: **settled 00:02 / law 31.** Assign to an **existing** sequence, or **create from a template**. Do not create the agent in Automations.
5. Word “event” — **settled 23:35 / law 28:** all objectives are events. C2b and Automations triggers are the same grain. Do not split them again.
6. Catalog of **in-system actions** besides enroll-agent. **Shape list (22:43):** [`PRIMITIVES.md`](./PRIMITIVES.md). Named: ascribe a tag · run an audit · who this applies to · make a form · **provision a firm**. Not “write any table.” Not webhook-as-an-action.
7. Seed §5.6 vs Hub-as-built vs the 20:24 definite-middle shape — **do not silently kill any of them**. Hub Rules are what to look at. Alignment is later.
9. Remaining output classes besides **required data** (law 23). Do not invent a full catalog this stamp. Hub-today vs lattice is A9 / A10.
10. **Listing of requested data on rule output + form bind** (law 25). Named 21:36 as not stood up in code. Mocked as A11–A12 (chrome) and A13 (diagram). Do not fill the listing in the product this stamp. Do not mint tables.
11. **Ant plate of the If node** — **drawn 01:20:** A15 (chain) · A16 (open). Hub still has the plant. A13 is still not this screen.
12. **Event catalog + global vs local** (law 27). **Drawn 18:53: A18.** **Shape list (22:43):** [`PRIMITIVES.md`](./PRIMITIVES.md). Form submitted (this form) · campaign failed · opt-out · firm created · audit finished · contact file imported · objective met. Not “any row changed.”
13. **Queryable lineage** (law 29). Agent-created vs hand-created objective → path → completion → time. Minimum: queryable. Do not mint a table from this sentence.
14. **Handle after the node** (law 33). Live walk does not hand the next node the module’s output. Do not treat editor preview as that. SA: do not circle pipe vs then-this — both are fine if the handle is real. Packet: [`SYSTEMS-AUTOMATIONS-NODE-OUTPUT.md`](./SYSTEMS-AUTOMATIONS-NODE-OUTPUT.md).

+# Pass 1 — Seed confirmation
+
+**Source:** `docs/register/SEED.md` at `c5bd617b9b1bb9fbd5d73c99da16a973594c6bd7`  
+**Law of Seed:** Everything we know, every assumption, every bet — product *and* how they get in. World is derived from this dump. Agents must not invent business facts outside it.  
+**Status in-repo:** Validated 2026-07-27. This pass **confirms**; it does not rewrite.
+
+## Product sentence (Seed §0.1)
+
+Immigration firms pay for an always-on system that engages dormant and active contacts, keeps immigration facts fresh through firm→client touchpoints, re-evaluates service eligibility as IRCC-shaped rules and client facts move, and surfaces when someone is campaign-worthy — so consultants book meetings without manually rechecking every file.
+
+Tower is **not** a reactive CRM. It is **proactive eligibility wrapped in engagement**.
+
+**One-line value:** Give us your contacts; we engage them, keep their immigration picture current, and surface when eligibility changes — without manually rechecking every file.
+
+## Growth sentence (Seed §0.2)
+
+Immigration consultancies convert into *running* Tower clients through **ALG** — not sales calls as the primary door, not self-serve onboarding forms — if one tap in a Meta feed makes a prepared campaign workspace legible, cheap public seed inputs provision that workspace, and an agent earns the hard inputs (database authorization + escrow) before the campaign actually runs.
+
+## Money posture (Seed §0.3, §7)
+
+Contingent cost. First ALG money door = **escrow** (firm↔Om Coda). End-clients pay Tower nothing. Credits and sales-call are **not** peer doors at activation. Escrow **release definition is a known unknown**.
+
+## Agent bet (Seed §0.4)
+
+Agent = presentation only (ask / explain / route). Automations and Wiring fulfill: scrape, instantiate, persist, fire, evaluate, OTP, money.
+
+## Core molecular outcomes already in Seed (application language)
+
+- **Core:** Tower automatically detects eligible candidates and initiates a campaign to get them to book a meeting. Eligible = service-eligible. Campaign = launch / nudge / reactivation. Success = meeting booked. Continuously while the firm has contacts and hands-free is armed.
+- **Access:** A consultant signs in and lands in their firm workspace.
+
+Later Function rewrote the consultant *outcome* so the consultant's verbs are hand-over · authorize · receive; machinery becomes leaf requirements. That is Outcomes cleanup (fork 1), not a Seed rewrite. Seed DNA stays.
+
+## Core loop (Seed §5)
+
+```
+Contacts / import
+  → Audit (reachability / sequence-start gate)
+  → Standard engagement (opt-in → re-engagement nudges → …)
+  → Collect & refresh Client Data via touchpoints
+  → Rule engine / Automations (re-evaluate eligibility)
+  → Nudges / escalations / reactivation / consultant signals
+  → Meeting booked
+  → (repeat as facts & rules move)
+```
+
+## Doctrine pins (Seed §16) — not dilutable
+
+1. Product bet = always-on eligibility + engagement → meeting booked.
+2. Growth bet = ALG Approach → forward-deploy activation → running desk.
+3. Activation sets target; acquisition fulfills seed quota.
+4. Finish lines are **input sets**.
+5. Forward-deploy ∈ activation; click budget ∈ acquisition only.
+6. Entry surfaces are product surfaces (Approach).
+7. One Approach per acquired non-operator persona.
+8. Ad = legibility; never persuade.
+9. Nudges = data collection; not spam.
+10. Audit = reachability; not sales ceremony.
+11. Engine 2: reactivation > nudge; one client, one motion.
+12. Agent presents; automation executes.
+13. Escrow-only door at activation payment moment.
+14. seed → world → acquisition → application → wiring (single Wiring).
+
+## Never invent (Seed §14) — hard stops for this experiment
+
+Public-before-contact end-client eligibility as Core. Agent seat. Full Client operator console. Operator as firm Board login. Credits/sales-call as peer activation doors. DB auth or escrow inside click budget. Forward-deploy as acquisition. Skip client opt-in because ALG. Cold email V1 Approach. Escrow as the only money forever. Officer POA / finder licensure / state disbursement as Tower gates. Sales assessment HTML as in-app Audit. Claiming live backend persistence or production ALG Approach as shipped.
+
+## Known unknowns the specification must keep open (Seed §13)
+
+1. Exact escrow terms / release outcome.  
+2. What “database authorization” means per practice stack.  
+3. Meta targeting / CAC.  
+4. Client desk depth.  
+5. D-01, D-02 (loop-closer builder).  
+6. Multi-consultant / roles / permissions.  
+7. CRM sync bidirectional.  
+8. When/whether email earns Meta entry.  
+9. Rule-pack IP / liability.  
+10. Production onboarding beyond seed manifests.  
+11. Evolution instrumentation.  
+12. Persistence target for workflows.  
+13. Rules UI: outcomes-toggle vs condition trees.  
+14. SMS/email consent regimes by geography.

+# Pass 3 — Machine track extract
+
+**Sources:** `docs/register/SYSTEMS-STORY.md` · `docs/register/SYSTEMS-REQUIREMENTS.md` · `docs/register/SYSTEMS-REQUIREMENTS-FILLED.md` · `docs/register/system-map/BUILD-system-map-v2-table-inventory.md` · `docs/register/DATA-IN-TABLES.md`  
+**Seat law:** Systems analyst locks substance in Story. Requirements **extract**; they do not invent.  
+**This pass does not promote:** `OPERATOR-REVISIONS.md`, `SYSTEMS-GOAL.md`, `SYSTEMS-OBJECTIVE-ESCROW.md` — denser than Seed/World, not Story musts until founder promotion.
+
+## Doctrine (from SYSTEMS-REQUIREMENTS.md)
+
+Tower is the **machine**. UI is only:
+
+| Extrusion | Job |
+|---|---|
+| **Control** | Injects a change into a state that already exists |
+| **Pane** | Displays a state the machine already has |
+
+Faceless triggers (email opened, window elapsed, reference version published) are native to this track. Outskirts maps cannot see them.
+
+## Spine the whole machine must continuously do
+
+While a firm has contacts and hands-free is armed:
+
+1. Keep engaging dormant and active contacts.
+2. Keep immigration-relevant facts fresh via firm→client touchpoints.
+3. Re-evaluate **service eligibility** as IRCC-shaped reference and client facts move.
+4. Surface campaign-worthy people so consultants book meetings without manually rechecking every file.
+
+Core pursuit: detect service-eligible candidates and initiate the right campaign motion (launch / nudge / reactivation) whose success event is **meeting booked**.
+
+Cross-cutting: Agent presentation ≠ fulfillment. House/open-box: evaluation, analysis, operational logic, and reference upkeep stay inspectable and changeable without a code deploy.
+
+## The twelve systems
+
+| # | System | Must fulfill |
+|---|---|---|
+| 1 | Acquisition (seed-capture) | Three cheap inputs inside click budget; return to scroll |
+| 2 | Provision / forward-deploy | No-login prepared workspace proving readiness, not value |
+| 3 | Commercial / hard-input | DB authorization + escrow; flip campaign to **running** |
+| 4 | Tenancy & access | Versioned manifests; OTP session; one desk either door |
+| 5 | Reachability / audit | Can we reach them and start a sequence? |
+| 6 | Consent / suppression | Opt-in; silenced when not opted in; DB auth ≠ consent |
+| 7 | Engagement / sequencing | **7a** campaign calendar · **7b** attempt / channel-ownership — never conflated |
+| 8 | Fact-refresh / data-collection | Nudges collect; field-class routing; write-back re-evaluates |
+| 9 | Reference-currency | Versioned IRCC-shaped tables as data; faceless trigger on move |
+| 10 | Eligibility re-evaluation | Private book; any-pathway; Analysis readout; every determination is a signal |
+| 11 | Signal / motion (Engine 2) | Record every detection; one motion by fixed precedence |
+| 12 | Meeting / loop-closer | meeting_booked → pending capture + live brief |
+
+## Must-not walls (selected, not exhaustive)
+
+- Pull DB auth or escrow into click budget; treat forward-deploy as acquisition; cold email V1 Approach.
+- Credits/sales-call as peer activation door; hold immigrant settlement funds.
+- Operator as firm Board login; Agent seat in admission.
+- Audit as scoring / ROI / sales ceremony.
+- Skip opt-in because ALG.
+- Document-dependent facts in forms.
+- Code deploy to update reference facts.
+- Public-before-contact end-client eligibility as Core.
+- Parallel motions for one client; Engine 2 replacing 7b inside a sequence.
+- Engagement record authoring motion.
+
+## Engine 2 precedence (system 11) — immutable
+
+1. Reactivation first, always, if anything is reactivation-worthy.
+2. Nudge only when nothing is reactivation-worthy.
+3. One nudge consolidates **every** outstanding self-reportable need into **one** form.
+4. When reactivation fires, secondary signals ride as **agenda** on the pre-meeting brief — never parallel outreach.
+5. **One client, one motion, ever.**
+
+**Silence inside this law:** what makes a signal **reactivation-worthy**. SME Handoff `elig-04` proposes a practice mechanism (material service-posture change). That is absorb, not a Story promotion. See `06-sme/` and `08-uncertainty/`.
+
+## Chain web (Story)
+
+```
+Acquisition --seed land--> Provision --prepared--> Commercial --running--> Application (5–12)
+Audit --sequence-ready--> Engagement enrollment
+7b finishing event --> arm next sequence
+Engagement nudge --> Fact-refresh
+Fact write-back --> Eligibility
+Reference move --> Eligibility
+Every determination --> Engine 2 signal --> motion --> Engagement
+meeting_booked --> pending capture write-back --> Eligibility (live brief)
+```
+
+Heartbeat: *seed → forward-deploy → run*, then self-feeding *detect → engage → collect → re-detect*, with Reference-currency injecting faceless external triggers.
+
+## Named states (Requirements extract, fused)
+
+Faceless-origin nodes (★) are first-class.
+
+`firm_tenancy` · `user_account` · `session` · `otp_challenge` · `firm_identity_binding` · `seed_capture` · `approach_impression`★ · `session_attribution` · `firm_public_facts`★ · `prepared_workspace` · `database_authorization` · `escrow_acceptance` / `escrow_terms` · `campaign_state`★ · `contact_record` · `reachability_verdict`★ · `sequence_ready` · `reachability_issue` · `consent_state`★ · `optin_phase` · `sequence_definition` · `phase_state` · `reactivation_arm_state` · `content_order` · `active_attempt`★ · `inbound_override`★ · `finishing_event`★ · `engagement_record`★ · `fact_ask` · `field_class_routing` · `fact_writeback`★ · `missing_fact_signal`★ · `reference_version`★★ · `constants_pack` · `eligibility_evaluation`★ · `eligibility_result`★ · `analysis_readout` · `evaluation_ruleset` · `signal`★ · `motion_decision`★ · `meeting_booked` · `pending_capture` · `live_brief`★
+
+Archetype faceless trigger: `reference_version` (a draw cutoff shifts with nobody present).
+
+## Table-first law (v2 inventory)
+
+The machine is **tables + a dumb runtime**.
+
+| Kind | Holds |
+|---|---|
+| **State** | Values/status the machine tracks |
+| **Rule** | When [trigger] + [condition] → change [target] to [value], as rows |
+| **Sequence / order** | Ordered, rearrangeable lists |
+
+Anything that should be modifiable must be a table. Frozen-in-prose that should vary is a bug unless it is a hard-gate / must-not / immutable wall.
+
+**Data in tables (Phase Two law, 18:44):** records that show in a module come from tables. Never hard-code data into the app. Missing table/field is Systems Analyst ascribe — do not invent a store in the SPA.
+

+
+These sit in `07-phase-two/` as **founder expansions parked**, and in `08-uncertainty/` as promotion gates — not as invented closures.

+Machine substance and spec extraction exist. Bind faces onto these states; do not discover more machine from screens.

+**Method:** `docs/sme/METHODOLOGY.md` · `docs/sme/DOCTRINE-sme-cto-implementation.md` §3 (compliance *modifies*)

+1. Immigration pathway / service-eligibility ops

+## Intended-product constraints this axis **modifies** (not new World seats)
+
+These are Handoff absorb targets. They are **not** founder-invented Seed closures. They **are** the practice residual Seed already crossed. Where Handoff still says NEEDS VERIFICATION, this spec keeps that marker.
+
+### Service eligibility (seat 1) — language the product must use
+
+- **Service-eligible** = firm-offered service family with positive B-* **and** a confidence tier — never “will get ITA” / CRS-competitive (`elig-03`).
+- Pathway pass may assert only after published version encodes program minima; non–EE base PNP is out-of-pack until stream rules are versioned (`elig-01`, `elig-02`).

+- **Reactivation-worthy (practice proposal for Story silence):** material service-posture change (new minima/category/draw clear, nomination/offer/cert, time-critical ops windows); missing self-reportables = nudge-only unless those windows fire (`elig-04`).  
+  **Promotion status:** this fills a Story **silence** with SME mechanism. It is **not** automatically Story must. Named in `08-uncertainty/` as absorb-vs-promotion.

+- Packs reference table keys/version pins only; reject numeric public-criteria literals (`ref-26`).

+
+- CEM triad (consent + ID + unsubscribe) hard-gates every firm-branded email **and** SMS (`casl-01`).

+- Cold “email the book for consent” forbidden (`casl-04`).

**Branch intent:** Resend CEM + Twilio SMS + Postgres CT stores + Resend webhooks

## Honesty

“Cut over” means client ports call `/wire` + `/auth` and server adapters exist. It does **not** mean:

# Surface intent — initiation vs view

**Parent doctrine:** [`DOCTRINE-sme-cto-implementation.md`](./DOCTRINE-sme-cto-implementation.md) §5  
**Audience:** PM functional design (and CTO when a no-face item earns a view window)  
**Status:** Standing method — derived from Tower implementation-pass inspection

---

## Principle

Not every implementation is an action, and "backend vs UI" is the wrong cut. Every implementation that earns a face is one of two types:

- **Initiation** — the human *acts*: open, authorize, bind, halt, trigger, provision. The affordance *does* something.
- **View / attribution / record** — the human *sees*: a status, a metric, an attribution, a record of what the machine did. No action; it is the operator's legible window into a mechanism.

Neither is "no UI." A view-only surface is a real, deliberate deliverable — often the operator's window into a backend capability (the open-box doctrine: the machine runs itself, but nothing is a black box). Deciding which type each implementation earns — or that it earns none — is the PM's (and, for its own surfaces, the CTO's) product judgment.

---

## Origin (failure prevented)

The implementation passes expressed *every* item as "On {Surface}, you can now…", which looked like a UI bias. On inspection it wasn't naïve: the backend mechanism was carried in the `Solution` field and ownership in `Handoff`. What the format lacked was a *view-vs-initiation* distinction and a "no immediate face" state. The correction is not "PM stops writing UI for CTO items" — it is that the PM is making a real surface-intent judgment (some things you *do*, some you only *see*), which is exactly what a good PM should decide.

---

## Mechanics

In functional design, classify each faced implementation as:

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `initiation` | Human acts; affordance does something |
| `view` | Human sees; window into a mechanism |
| `none` | No immediate face — hand to Wiring |

This axis is not SME-only — it applies to the **persona/function side too**, and already operates implicitly there:

| Surface | Intent |
|---|---|
| Board | view / inhabit |

# Operator — Activation & forward-deploy

**Kind:** secondary *(candidate co-core — ALG onramp)*  
**Subject:** Operator (house-global + per-firm staging)

**Statement**
> As Operator, I can stage a no-login prepared workspace for a captured firm from house templates and
> public facts, walk the firm through readiness, and secure its database authorization and escrow —
> so that the Consultant reaches a running desk.

---

## Root — outcome

**Clarity:** *(statement)*  
**Criteria — when:** After seed inputs land (ALG) for a captured firm.  
**Conditions:** House templates + public facts suffice for readiness proof; hard inputs still earned.

---

## Depth 1 — first How

**Q:** How do I stage a no-login prepared workspace for a captured firm from house templates and public facts, walk the firm through readiness, and secure its database authorization and escrow?

**Clarity:** Starting from Activation & forward-deploy, click **In-flight activations**; on a captured firm row, click **Forward-deploy**, select a published Engagement template version, type public firm-facts and brand package fields, click **Hydrate**, then click **Readiness walkthrough** on Prepared Workspace; view Authorize book and Accept terms completion chips on Activation state **Progress** before the firm is running.

**DNA for children:**
1. forward-deploy a Prepared Workspace from house templates and public facts
2. walk readiness with the firm
3. secure database authorization plus escrow acceptance

---

### Leaf 1.1 — forward-deploy Prepared Workspace

**Q:** How do I forward-deploy a Prepared Workspace from house templates and public facts?

**Clarity:** Starting from Activation & forward-deploy, click **In-flight activations**. On a captured firm row, click **Forward-deploy**. On the forward-deploy form, select a published Engagement template version from the **Template version** dropdown, type public firm-facts and brand package fields, then click **Hydrate** (primary button). Hydrate writes staged Prepared Workspace state read by Prepared Workspace and Activation state Progress (forward-deployed row). Backend enriches/scrapes public facts autonomously after Hydrate — no Meta/ESP affordances in Tower; view staging status chips on In-flight activations if shown. No client PII required yet.

**Criteria — when:** Seed inputs landed.

+## 1. What Tower is
+
+**Company:** Om Coda. **Buyer:** immigration consultancies (B2B firm operators). **V1 geography/program shape:** Canadian immigration pathways (Express Entry / CEC / FSW / FST / PNP and related). Other countries are not forbidden later; they are a founder-only geography expansion.
+
+**Product bet:** Firms pay for an always-on system that engages dormant and active contacts, keeps immigration facts fresh through firm→client touchpoints, re-evaluates **service eligibility** as IRCC-shaped rules and client facts move, and surfaces when someone is campaign-worthy — so consultants book meetings without manually rechecking every file.
+
+Tower is **proactive eligibility wrapped in engagement**. It is not a reactive CRM, not a public finder of end-clients, not a money transmitter of immigrant funds, not an Agent desk (Agent is a feature), not a full end-client operator console in V1.
+
+**Growth bet (ALG):** One tap in a Meta feed yields name + website + phone/email inside a click budget; the system forward-deploys a no-login prepared campaign under the firm’s identity; an agent (presentation only) earns database authorization and escrow; then the campaign **runs**. Assisted / operator-led entry (OLG) remains a real second door into the **same** application.
+
+**Agency shape:** Om Coda runs Tower across firms. Evaluation rules, analysis, operational logic, engagement templates, and reference upkeep belong to an **operator/house** layer — inspectable and changeable without a code deploy (open box). The firm inhabits the book and the meetings. Firms do **not** author packs. House authors; tenancy binds.
+
+**One-line value:** Give us your contacts; we engage them, keep their immigration picture current, and surface when eligibility changes — without manually rechecking every file.
+

+| **Application** | Desk performing once running | Continuously toward **meeting booked** |
+| **Evolution** | Register-driven product change | Not a client lifecycle phase |

One Approach per acquired non-house party (V1: Consultant). Engagement contacts are never acquired via Approach. House is never acquired via Approach.
+
+**Contingent cost:** First ALG money door is **escrow** (firm↔Om Coda). Credits and sales-call are not peer doors at that moment. End-clients pay Tower nothing. Detection is free to the contact. **Escrow release definition is unspecified** (named silence).

+## 5. The machine (twelve systems)
+
+UI is not the system. The system must pre-exist the UI. Faceless events are first-class.
+
+### 5.1 What the whole machine must continuously do
+
+While a firm has contacts and hands-free is armed: engage · refresh facts · re-evaluate service eligibility · surface campaign-worthy people toward **meeting booked**.
+
+### 5.2 Systems
+
+1. **Acquisition** — Meta Approach; one-click constraint; legible output; continue-scroll; persist/attribute capture. Must not pull DB auth or escrow into the click budget; must not treat forward-deploy as acquisition; no cold-email V1 Approach.
+2. **Provision / forward-deploy** — On seed land, scrape **public** firm facts, instantiate **Om Coda** methodology templates (launch → re-engagement → reactivation), serve no-login prepared workspace. Must not derive the campaign from the private book before authorization.
+3. **Commercial / hard-input** — Land DB authorization + escrow; flip `campaign_state` to **running**. Escrow only as peer door. No immigrant settlement funds.
+4. **Tenancy & access** — Versioned seed manifests; passwordless OTP; unprovisioned email → generic 200, no code; ALG and OLG land in one session matrix.
+5. **Reachability / audit** — One question: can we reach them and start a sequence? Verdicts reachable / partial / unreachable. Sequence-ready gates enrollment. Not scoring, not ROI, not sales ceremony.
+6. **Consent / suppression** — Opt-in before deep collection; silenced when not opted in or when opted out. Firm DB auth ≠ end-client consent.
+7. **Engagement / sequencing** — Two engines, never conflated:
+   - **7a Campaign calendar** — day-ordered content under Engine 2 precedence.
+   - **7b Attempt / channel-ownership** — one owning channel at a time; waits nest under the failed owner; forward-only when criteria met; live inbound can override; finishing event closes and can arm the next. Engagement **record** authors nothing.
+8. **Fact-refresh** — Nudges collect. Field class: self-reportable → forms; document-dependent → **never** a form (Manage); employer-directed → firm. Any write-back → immediate re-evaluation. Missing fact → signal.
+9. **Reference-currency** — Versioned IRCC-shaped tables as **data**. A reference move is a faceless trigger. No code deploy to update facts.
+10. **Eligibility re-evaluation** — Private book only. Trigger → Constants → Conditions → Rules → structured output. Pathway pass = **any** pathway assertion, not one favoured pathway. Analysis readout with machine output retained. Every determination (including missing-data) is a signal. Open-box.
+11. **Engine 2 (signal / motion)** — Record every detection. Decide outreach separately: reactivation first; nudge only otherwise; one form consolidating all outstanding self-reportables; secondary signals as brief agenda; **one client, one motion, ever**.
+12. **Meeting / loop-closer** — `meeting_booked` is the success event. Outstanding self-reportables → pending capture. Write-back → re-evaluate. Brief is **live**, not a snapshot.
+
+### 5.3 Self-feeding ring
+
+```
+seed_capture → firm_public_facts → prepared_workspace
+  → (database_authorization + escrow_acceptance) → campaign_state=running
+      → reachability → sequence_ready → engagement
+      → fact_ask / fact_writeback ─┐
+      reference_version ───────────┼→ eligibility_evaluation → signal → motion_decision
+                                   │                              ↓
+                                   └──────── missing_fact_signal ←┘
+meeting_booked → pending_capture → fact_writeback → live_brief (recompute)
+```
+
+Faceless injectors: `reference_version`, `fact_writeback` / `missing_fact_signal`, time/threshold criteria inside `active_attempt`, inbound override.
+
+### 5.4 Table-first
+
+The machine is **tables + a dumb runtime**. Kinds: **state | rule | sequence**. Anything that should be modifiable is a table. Runtime holds no content. Records that appear in a module come from tables — never hard-coded into the app.
+
+### 5.5 Hard human gates the machine must not automate away
+
+Seed capture · assisted provision · OTP · database authorization · escrow accept · client consent / not silenced · meeting booking · firm refusal of illegal/unethical outreach.

+## 7. Operator authorship grain (Phase Two, without overwriting Seed)
+
+### 7.1 Agents (engagement authorship) — flagship 15:43
+
+The operator defines outreach **sequencing** (sequence **and** the order it is deployed), **per firm or as a default** plus overrides; **escalation between attempts** (retry / attempt rules); and a **goal / goal criteria** that is itself an **escalation point** — to another agent, to a workflow, or it ends. Once met, met. Everything in the middle is modular.
+
+App-facing container (does not replace the flag):
+
+- **Sequence** = blank canvas that can hold multiple **campaigns**.
+- **Campaign** = one **objective**. First thing on a campaign is the objective.
+- Untemplated objective = binary event (happened or it didn’t), then named. Templated objective populates the campaign.
+- Sequence templates (opt-in / re-engagement / reactivation) ≠ objective templates.
+- Channels = medium. Channel rules = escalation on that medium. Attempt = cycle of the same sequence. Attempt rules are not at the channel.
+- Sequencing (how many channels, order) at campaign level. Content inside the channel node.
+- **Override this** reveals channel nodes as wires. Rules nest like CSS (global → sequence → campaign → channel).
+- Empty world: no templates until authored.
+- Agents enroll **starts the mission now**. Automations enroll waits on an event.
+
+Three layers that must all be specified: **authorship** · **record** · **unattended runtime**. A pretty editor whose Activity pane lies after the operator leaves has failed.
+
+**Parked (not Story must):** goal = completion of an objective; classes of sequence are classes of objective; goals-as-escalation-events between campaigns. Packet 022’s mechanism (objective met as Local event; escalation as **subscription** to `objective_met`; no destination column / no `goal` table required) is **settled as mechanism** and still awaits Story §7 **wording** promotion. This spec records both facts and does not promote.
+
+**Call** appears on the face because the founder asked to see the node. The machine still has **form**. Do not drop form.

+### 7.2 Automations (operations brain) — entered from Agents outskirts
+
+On this **event** (schedule or trigger, Global or Local) → perform this **operation** → on this kind of result do X / on that kind do Y. DAG. Smallest workflow = trigger · rule · action. Canvas can chain.
+
+- Forms / data requests are created **here**, not in Agents.
+- A data request is already an origin event for Agents (recursive join).
+- Automations does **not** author a new agent. Assign existing, or from a template. Select agent = whole sequence.
+- Rule = composite of conditions + constants; togglable outcome families; GUI default, named-code escape; industry-modular.
+- Rule output may include re-engagement and/or reactivation **signals** and a **required-data listing**. Forms bind to that listing. Deterministic: no AI to decide required fields.
+- Two condition grains: inside the rule vs If node on previous result. Do not collapse.
+- All objectives are events. Write-back **is** the event. No special return wire.
+- Campaign failure is an event. In-app actions include ascribe a tag, run an audit, make a form (shape list — not a complete catalog).
+- After a node: **every write that run made**. Next node picks. That is the primitive. Walker 015 is the live walk; this spec does not recut it.

+
+**Do:** send people to a goal (Agents) · do a named in-app thing (tag, audit, form, …). Not “write whatever table.”

# Wiring — how we build it (method notes)

## Preface

These notes come at a specific moment. We had already run the Register all the way down for Tower — Seed, World, personas, outcomes, How-trees, and both SME passes (the practice/compliance axis via the Engagement Manager, and the capability axis via the CTO). Implementations existed. What we did not yet have was the Wiring: the backend layer with no face. When we sat down to build it, we hit a wall — we assumed we'd gather everything that must exist, organize it, then draw the canvas. That order broke, because organizing-first forces you to declare what a "flow" and a "trigger" are, and trigger-ness turned out to be relational, not intrinsic: the same node triggers in one path and is an interim step in another. This doc is the inversion we arrived at — trace each implementation one at a time, the same way we build UI, and let the structure fall out of the graph rather than imposing it up front. It also carries the deeper thing that surfaced along the way: that anchoring wiring to events rather than UI arrangement is what finally lets the technical layer run without design breaking the click-path underneath it.

---

**What this is.** The method for producing Tower's Wiring: the CTO/technical layer that has no face.
It is the backend twin of how we build UI — we do not design the whole system top-down, we **trace
each implementation one at a time** and let the structure assemble itself. This doc is the formula;
the companion [`NODE-DEFINITION.md`](./NODE-DEFINITION.md) defines what a node is (referenced throughout);
[`WIRING-CRITICAL-INTERACTION.md`](./WIRING-CRITICAL-INTERACTION.md) defines which interactions count as origins that land on those nodes.

**Governing stance:** *connect first, classify later.* We never decide what a "flow," a "trigger," or
a "category" is before the graph exists. Those are labels you read *off* a finished graph, never
inputs to building it.

---

## 1. The failure node (why we don't organize first)

The instinct is: "look at everything that must exist, categorize it, then draw the canvas." That path
fails, and here is exactly where:

Organizing-first forces you to declare what a **flow** is, which forces you to declare what a
**trigger** is. But **trigger-ness is not a property of a node — it is a property of a node's role in
a particular path.** The same step is an interim step in one implementation and the trigger in
another. Any scheme that asks "is this a trigger?" globally breaks, because the honest answer is
"depends which path you're looking at." You cannot pre-classify something whose identity is
relational. So we invert: **trace, don't classify.**

---

## 2. The unit of work: the traced implementation

We go **one implementation at a time** — the same discipline as building a UI click-path, moved to
the backend. The unit is the *traced implementation*, not "the designed system."

For each implementation, walk it with one simple, repeating rule (the exact mirror of "where are we
starting from?" in UI):

1. **Where do we start from?** Is the first thing this implementation touches an **existing** node (a
   table/system already on the canvas) or a **new** one we must create? (Node = see [`NODE-DEFINITION.md`](./NODE-DEFINITION.md).)
2. **What's the next thing — for this specific use case?** Given this implementation, what does that
   first node's event touch next? Existing node or new node? Determine it.
3. **Connect them in event language:** *when X happens in system A, this happens in system B.* The
   edge is the event and its ripple, stated in plain language — not code, not the operating language.
4. **Hang the non-structural constraints on the edge:** *…within X ms · idempotent · encrypted ·
   under this jurisdiction.* These are the things the topology can't express (see §6).

# Wiring — what a node is (node definition)

## Preface

This doc is the companion the Wiring Method leans on. The moment we decided to trace implementations into a graph, one question had to be answered before anything else: what counts as a node? We nearly settled for "a table or a system," but "system" was too coarse and "table" too narrow on its own — so we pushed until we found the actual discriminator, which is altitude, not technology. The breakthrough was noticing what a table *is* relative to SQL — the named state one rung above the language that operates on it — and realizing that relationship generalizes to every system. We cemented it by running the same Postgres-on-Supabase stack through three events and watching the node land at three different rings (table, engine, platform) purely by what the event acted on. That test is what turned a rule of thumb into something load-bearing, and it's why this sits beside the method rather than inside it: the method connects nodes, but only if we agree, precisely, on what a node is.

---

**What this is.** The definition of a node on the Wiring graph — the thing the [`WIRING-METHOD.md`](./WIRING-METHOD.md)
formula connects. Getting this altitude right is what keeps the graph in plain event language and out
of code. Read this before tracing anything.

**Counterpart (origins):** [`WIRING-CRITICAL-INTERACTION.md`](./WIRING-CRITICAL-INTERACTION.md) — which user interactions count as writes that land on a node.

---

## 1. The rule

> **A node is the smallest *named unit of state* that an event can happen to, sitting exactly one
> layer above the language or mechanics that operate on it.**

It's the **noun that gets acted on**, never the **verb that does the acting**. You point at it, say
"this changed," and mean something — without writing a single line of the operating language.

**The reference instance — table vs SQL.** SQL is *how you operate on* a table; the table is the
*named unit of state* the operations act on. The table is the addressable noun; SQL is the verb layer
underneath. You work at the noun. That relationship — **state one rung above its operating
language** — is what we look for in every other system to find its node altitude.

---

## 2. The test (both directions)

The property that makes "table" right is that **you never have to get down into the operating
language** to name it. Use that as the test, both ways:

- **If you can only name the node in its operating language, go DOWN a rung.** ("Supabase" or "the
  system" is too coarse — many unrelated events touch it indistinctly and the ripples vanish inside

# Operator revisions — shape bets that explain Tower’s open box

**As of:** 2026-07-28  
**Status:** Living notes — not World seats, not SME answers. Prefer under-claim.  
**Join:** [`SEED.md`](./SEED.md) · Console purpose popovers · `guidelines/Reactivation.md` · methodology gap §6

This file holds **operator-facing product shape bets** that are easy to miss if you only read seats and admission. They explain *why Hub looks modular and inspectable* — and where that tooling should eventually live.

---

## 1. Domain modularity bet (still on the table)

Tower’s evaluation stack was shaped so the **same software** could serve another vertical with a similar shape (always-on eligibility + engagement over a private book), by swapping industry packs rather than forking the product.

| Surface of the bet | What you see in product |
|--------------------|-------------------------|
| **Automations → Constants** | Industry folders (Immigration rich; Legal / Financial / Insurance placeholders) — versioned criteria, not hard-coded one-offs |
| **Automations → Rules** | Pre-packaged evaluators that compose constants + industry conditions (open, inspectable — not a sealed black box) |
| **Analysis** | Human-readable outcomes from those rules |

**Cosmetic / pack changes** may be required per segment; the **graph shape** (Trigger → If / Rules → Actions that enroll Agents) is meant to stay.

---

## 2. Open-box evaluation law (standing)

For any Om Coda product that **evaluates data to decide or analyze**, prefer an **open box**: operators can see and change the operations that produce answers without a code deploy for every tweak.

**Where it should sit:** not as everyday consultant chrome forever. Target shape is an **agency / operator / admin view** that configures evaluation for everyone under that tenancy. Today’s Hub (Audits, Agents, Automations) is historically parked inside the firm workspace because Tower was built under managed / OLG-style thinking — that placement is a **revision candidate**, not the destination.

---

## 3. Audit — what it actually is

Audit is **not** a vague “compliance sweep” and **not** sales ROI ceremony.

| In | Out |
|----|-----|
| On / after **import**: email valid, phone valid, channel match to intended sequence, dedupe, already-in-Tower, consent/silenced, name present | Pathway scoring, CRS, activation probability, PASS/FAIL sales theater |
| Answer: *can we reach them, and can we start a sequence?* | Minimum contact-count gates |

# Capability SME — considerations · solutions · implementation

**Status:** Paper only — **not** absorbed into Register twins, HANDOFF, or CT plant.  
**Downstream (paper Wiring):** CTO Think Stack steps 1–4 filed under [`../../wiring/paper-trace/`](../../wiring/paper-trace/) — Function traces / Can’ts / Furnish / node buckets. Still awaiting human validation before absorb.  
**Axis:** Capability (“who knows **how to accomplish** X”), not compliance (“who is responsible for X”).  
**Roster source:** [`00-ROSTER.md`](./00-ROSTER.md) (C1–C7)  
**Methodology:** [`../METHODOLOGY.md`](../METHODOLOGY.md) — Pass2 `<mechanism> so that <purpose>` + PM implementation bridge (`implementationProblem` / `implementation` / `implementationAdds`)  
**Surface vocab:** [`../implementation/00-SURFACE-VOCAB.md`](../implementation/00-SURFACE-VOCAB.md)  
**Compliance seats (do not confuse):** [`../ROSTER.md`](../ROSTER.md) seats 1–7 — already shipped; this package **adds** capability seats beside them.

---

## How to validate

1. Read [`00-ROSTER.md`](./00-ROSTER.md) for why each seat exists and which surfaces it reveals (`exists` / `partial` / `new`).
2. Review each seat file below (Pass2 + implementation interleaved per item — same shape as compliance CASL combined writing).

+
+## Identity
+
+- Contestant: **omcoda** (Contestant 2)
+- Isolated: did not look for other contestants’ work
+- Tower application code: read-only; no product implementation; no `git push`; no PRs/issues
+- Preservation root: `/home/ubuntu/tower-spec-output/`

+- Stop (UTC, recorded): `2026-10-19T16:52:00Z` approximately (see STATUS.json write)
+
+## Initial approach
+
+The assignment named Omcoda methodology and forbade substituting Spec Kit / OpenSpec / BMad. The repository’s own front door (`docs/README.md` orientation path) and `docs/register/PASS-FORK-MAP.md` already state the operating spine:
+
+```
+Seed → World → Systems Story → Systems Requirements → (∥ Personas & Function)
+  → bind extrusions → SME → Enrichment → Furnish → Wiring → CT Plant → Translation
+```
+
+Two-column synthesis (`docs/method/TWO-COLUMN-SYNTHESIS.md`) is the join. Decision constitution forbids catch-all TBD and names a short founder-only class — so the pass could proceed without asking the coordinator for requirements.
+
+I did **not** treat “complete specification” as rewriting Seed/World (they are validated/derived) or as filling known unknowns. I treated it as walking the spine, stating the **intended** product those locked passes already commit to, folding capability *additions* that practice could not see, including Phase Two founder wording without overwriting 15:43 or promoting parked expansions, and putting every remaining hole in a named gate.
+
+Phase Two was read **after** Phase One spine so module flags could not replace Seed.
+
+## First substantive artifacts
+
+1. `00-session/SESSION-START.md` — SHA, constraints, sequence.
+2. `00-session/METHODOLOGY-INVENTORY.md` (+ `.v1.md` freeze) — method docs actually used, by path.
+3. `00-session/WORKING-PLAN.md` — method-determined order and stop rule.
+4. `01-seed/SEED-CONFIRMATION.md` — dump confirmation, never-invent, KUs.
+5. `02-world/WORLD-CONFIRMATION.md` — ecosystem sentence, finish lines, quarantine of WORLD-CRAFT-ARCHIVE.
+
+These exist so evolution can be examined: later specs cite them rather than silently mutating Seed.
+
+## Later revisions / discoveries
+
+- **Outcomes fork already solved.** Consultant core is hand-over · authorize · receive; engagement machinery is leaf requirement on operator modules. Re-deriving “consultant engages” would violate How law.
+- **Story vs Phase Two tension is already named in-repo.** 15:43 goal-as-escalation is founder wording (face). `SYSTEMS-GOAL.md` is durable expansion **not** Story must until promoted. Packet 022 settles a *mechanism* (objective_met as Local event; escalation as subscription) without changing the wording rule. The spec records both and does not promote.
+- **Capability Register absorb is not started** (`docs/sme/capability/00-ROSTER.md`, `CAPABILITY-CONSIDERATIONS.md`). Doctrine says capability *adds* and must be folded before build. Folding those homes into *this* specification (Sending infrastructure, Conversations, pipelines) while marking in-repo How as unabsorbed is the method-correct move. Omitting them would recreate the CTO sink.
+- **Hub vs Ant vs Configuration libraries** looks like a conflict and is not, if Ant is the translation of operator libraries and Hub is plant/reference. Treating Hub as the app would violate Phase Two law.
+- **Prototype honesty ≠ intended product.** Seed §11 and GO-CUTOVER describe as-built. Using them to shrink ALG/escrow/eligibility intent would violate Seed §14 (never claim shipped, and never delete the bet).
+- **v2 of the primary spec** only added §13 (Enrichment / Furnish / Wiring / Operator-revisions grade). v1 preserved at `SPEC/TOWER-INTENDED-PRODUCT.v1.md`.
+
+## How I decided what to do next
+
+At each step the next artifact was the next spine node, not a coordinator checklist:
+
+| After | Next because |
+|---|---|
+| Method inventory | Seed (dump) |
+| Seed | World (derivation) |
+| World | Parallel: Story/Requirements **and** Outcomes/How |
+| Both tracks | Bind / two-column join |
+| Bind | Practice SME absorb (modifies) then capability absorb (adds) |
+| SME | Phase Two module flags (same method, micro) |
+| Flags | Named gates/silences (decision constitution) |
+| Silences | Downstream Enrichment/Furnish/Wiring (spine remainder that does not change identity) |
+| Downstream | Primary spec + bundle + STATUS |

+I did not fetch unpinned pull refs as product law. `docs/README.md` points at PRs #86/#96/#110 for live packets; the experiment pins SHA `c5bd617`. Product facts used are those **in the snapshot**. Mentions of those PRs in-repo are recorded as in-document pointers, not as fetched extra founder decisions.

Filling escrow release, D-01/D-02, multi-consultant roles, or a `goal` table from chrome would invent founder decisions.
